facts.claim: The server is the PyPI package mcp-server-fetch (latest 2026.10.10, uploaded 2026-10-11), run with uvx and no arguments.
facts.evidence: README: command uvx, args ["mcp-server-fetch"]; PyPI info.version 2026.10.10, not yanked.

facts.claim: One tool, fetch(url, max_length=5000, start_index=0, raw=false); read-only, can reach any internet host.
facts.evidence: Fetches a URL and returns its contents as markdown.

facts.claim: Flags: --ignore-robots-txt (robots.txt otherwise obeyed for model-initiated requests), --allow-private-ips (disables the private/loopback/link-local guard), --user-agent=, --proxy-url (else HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY).
facts.evidence: --allow-private-ips: Turns off the guard that blocks private, loopback, and link-local addresses.

facts.claim: Security: server may reach internal addresses; default guard blocks private/loopback/link-local/metadata (e.g. 169.254.169.254) and checks redirects, but does not protect against DNS rebinding and does not check hosts only a proxy resolves.
facts.evidence: does not protect against DNS rebinding

facts.claim: Maintained in modelcontextprotocol/servers (src/fetch), listed as a current reference server, not archived. No official npm equivalent: the npm registry returned 404 for @modelcontextprotocol/server-fetch.
facts.evidence: npm 404; GitHub README lists only uvx, pip and docker.

choices.because: official server is a PyPI package; no official npm package exists
it makes requests from the user's machine to arbitrary URLs (SSRF, prompt injection steering); the built-in guard has documented gaps

choices.decision: no smoke op and no network.hosts
choices.because: the only tool needs a URL; destinations are arbitrary by design

open: Fetch pin rests on PyPI plus README (README shows unpinned).
The --allow-private-ips flag and the private-address guard appear in the current README only; whether they exist in 2026.10.10 specifically was not checked in source.
Tool schema read from the README only; no tools/list check.
network.hosts omitted deliberately; LOTR cannot restrict destinations for this server.
Whether the consent glob 'fetch' also matches the prompt named fetch was not examined.
